lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Meal Planning, Cooking, and Food Management
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: shopping lists and unit costs

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic shopping lists and unit costs task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Using a printed sample price table for three products, each shown in two or three different package sizes with a listed price, the learner calculates which size is the better value for each product and then writes a shopping list for a five-dinner week, grouping every item under the store section where it would be found.
materials: learner-local: calculator or scratch paper for division

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Name one item where choosing the larger size instead of the smaller size would have been a mistake for a five-dinner week, and explain why using the numbers.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Unit-cost calculation: All unit costs are calculated correctly and the better-value size is correctly identified for each product. | Shopping list organization: All items are correctly grouped under the four store-section headings and match the planned dinners. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner recalculate the shopping list for a ten-dinner week instead of five, and explain which package-size choices change and which stay the same.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic shopping lists and unit costs task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: calculator or scratch paper for division

resources.title: shopping lists and unit costs worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Using a printed sample price table for three products, each shown in two or three different package sizes with a listed price, the learner calculates which size is the better value for each product and then writes a shopping list for a five-dinner week, grouping every item under the store section where it would be found.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact shopping lists and unit costs decision or action.
Model move 2: Look at the sample price table before doing any math.
Model move 3: For each of the three sample products, divide the listed price by the size to find the unit cost, then circle the better-value size for each one.

Model check: Unit-cost calculation: All unit costs are calculated correctly and the better-value size is correctly identified for each product. | Shopping list organization: All items are correctly grouped under the four store-section headings and match the planned dinners.

resources.title: shopping lists and unit costs action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for shopping lists and unit costs.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: shopping lists and unit costs coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Using a printed sample price table for three products, each shown in two or three different package sizes with a listed price, the learner calculates which size is the better value for each product and then writes a shopping list for a five-dinner week, grouping every item under the store section where it would be found.
Coach direction: Look at the sample price table before doing any math.
Learner prompt: Without calculating, guess which size of the rice product looks like the better deal, and explain what made you guess that.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: shopping lists and unit costs complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each of the three sample products, divide the listed price by the size to find the unit cost, then circle the better-value size for each one.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I calculated a unit cost for every package size listed in the table, not just one size per product.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I circled the size with the lower unit cost for each of the three products.
Response 3 (t2-p3): Was the size with the better unit cost the same size you guessed in the warm-up? If not, what changed your answer?
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: shopping lists and unit costs minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Name one item where choosing the larger size instead of the smaller size would have been a mistake for a five-dinner week, and explain why using the numbers.

Success checks: Unit-cost calculation: All unit costs are calculated correctly and the better-value size is correctly identified for each product. | Shopping list organization: All items are correctly grouped under the four store-section headings and match the planned dinners.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: shopping lists and unit costs supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional shopping lists and unit costs condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Unit-cost calculation: All unit costs are calculated correctly and the better-value size is correctly identified for each product. | Shopping list organization: All items are correctly grouped under the four store-section headings and match the planned dinners..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: shopping lists and unit costs — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the shopping lists and unit costs task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.

retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
